analysis:
This batch contains only CHANGELOG.md head text, in two units (lines 1-203 and 204 onward). The file is documentation, so the changes add no executable attack surface and no direct security regression. The diff itself was not supplied, only the resulting text. I therefore could not tell which entries are new and read the file for claims that touch security.

The top 'update and restart relaunch' entry (#1306) says `darkbloom update` and `darkbloom restart` now wait up to 60 s for launchd, and that a failed relaunch re-arms the watchdog when auto-restart is on. That touches the provider lifecycle and the watchdog/rollback authority in T-043 and TB-003. The implementing code is not in this batch. A reviewer of the provider source should check that the re-arm path does not weaken the update, rollback or signed-bundle checks.

The other entries (Autopilot, the cache routing persistence, the 30-minute SSD TTL under SEC-035/T-041, App Attest protocol 3 only under TB-011/T-052 to T-058, the removal of the unauthenticated earnings lookup under T-031) describe changes made elsewhere. They are consistent with the canonical threat model and are not evidence of a new weakness. The 30-minute TTL and fixed 20 GiB reserve statements match T-041. The T-031 closure is described as complete. The changelog also lists the coordinator-side floor `EIGENINFERENCE_MIN_PROVIDER_VERSION` as a manual live-deploy step. That is an operational note, not a code issue.

No findings. Coverage is limited to the changelog text; the claimed code changes behind it were not reviewed here.
